headline: Attribution, perturbation and long-read methods ground regulatory epigenomic inference
label: Computational Methods For Regulatory Epigenomics
summary: Long-read, single-cell and deep-learning approaches now link chromatin state, enhancers and splicing to variant and expression effects.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational inference of regulatory state from multi-modal genomic data, with predictions increasingly tied to perturbations and explicit structure. Several items infer directed or interpretable networks: causal discovery over radiation perturbations and RNA-seq yields directed gene networks, and REGA uses reference regulatory element catalogs to infer TF-RE-gene programs and GRNs. ENCODE-rE2G provides an encyclopedia of 92M enhancer-gene interactions across 369 cell types, benchmarked against CRISPR and eQTL data. Epigenomic state is linked to downstream readouts elsewhere: chromatin states shape cfDNA fragmentation in TEANA, and RIDDLER detects single-cell CNVs across scATAC-seq and methylation assays. Population-scale and single-cell variant mapping, including TOPMed e/sQTLs and scHi-HOST under influenza infection, extends this to causal variant prioritization. What is new is the use of reference catalogs and perturbation-anchored causal structure to move from association toward mechanism.
